reason: Exact match. A filament-sheath is the united filaments forming a sheath, which is what the staminal tube class (FLOPO_0986013) covers: the fused filaments of two or more stamens. The previous review added that class, so no new class is needed. Length and 'curved' apply to it as they do to a staminal tube.

This is a specialised spine-forming cell. The phrase '1-15 spine-cells on each side' suggests an alga or a bryophyte. It comes from one flora only. The only possible target is native plant cell (PO_0025606), and that is too broad to keep the meaning. PO has no specific class for it, and one flora does not justify a new class. Without more context the structure is unclear.

Approximate, not exact: the flora's phrase is broader than gemma. In a bryophyte flora, 'asexual reproductive bodies' that are uniseriate, filamentous and multicellular are gemmae. PO defines gemma (PO_0025614) narrowly, as a small ball of cells on a thallus, so filamentous moss gemmae fit that definition only loosely. It is still the nearest PO class; the alternative, fruit (PO_0009001, which lists 'propagule' as a synonym), would be wrong. The bearer is the gemma; 'present' is a presence statement about it.

A petalodium is the petal-like appendage of a cyathial gland in Euphorbia. It is a real structure, but neither PO nor FLOPO has a class for the cyathial gland or its appendage. The only related class is cyathium (FLOPO_0985029), and pattern 12 (part of a qualified whole) cannot express an appendage of a gland of a cyathium. It occurs in one flora only, so a new class is not justified yet. If more floras use it, consider a new class 'cyathial gland appendage' as part of cyathium.
